name: Florence Cathedral (Duomo)
overview: The Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, commonly known as the Duomo, is Florence's iconic cathedral famous for its magnificent Renaissance dome designed by Filippo Brunelleschi. It's a masterpiece of Italian Gothic architecture and engineering.
history: This cathedral represents the triumph of Renaissance engineering over medieval limitations. When construction began in 1296, architects planned a massive dome but had no idea how to build it! For over 100 years, the cathedral sat unfinished with a gaping hole where the dome should be. Then came Filippo Brunelleschi, a goldsmith-turned-architect who studied Roman ruins and devised an ingenious double-shell dome design. Without using temporary wooden supports (impossible at this height), he built the first major dome since ancient Rome's Pantheon. His revolutionary techniques included a herringbone brick pattern and hidden chains for support. The dome became the symbol of Florence's wealth and power during the Renaissance, inspiring Michelangelo's St. Peter's dome in Rome. Remarkably, we still don't fully understand all of Brunelleschi's engineering secrets - some of his techniques remain mysteries even today!
highlights: Brunelleschi's Dome - first dome built since antiquity without temporary wooden supports
463 steps to climb to the top of the dome for panoramic city views
Stunning façade of white, pink, and green marble in geometric patterns
Vasari and Zuccaro's frescoes of the Last Judgment inside the dome
tips: Book timed entry tickets online for dome climb. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees). Dome climb is strenuous and not recommended for those with claustrophobia or heart conditions. Best views from Piazzale Michelangelo at sunset.
